001.name: Rule of Thirds Composition
001.summary: Divide the frame evenly into a 3×3 grid with two horizontal and two vertical lines, placing the subject on the intersections or lines for a more natural, dynamic composition.

points.title: Subject on Intersections
points.body: The four intersections act as focal points that naturally draw the viewer's eye.

points.title: Balanced Whitespace
points.body: Distribute space thoughtfully so the layout can breathe and feel refined.

points.title: Visual Guidance
points.body: Lines and elements guide the eye, strengthening rhythm and direction.

usage.title: Usage Tips
items: Landscape / Architecture: place the horizon along the upper or lower third line
Portrait / Still Life: align the subject with an intersection or third line
Creative Design: break the rule intentionally to create tension

002.name: Golden Ratio Composition
002.summary: The Golden Ratio (1:1.618) is a principle of harmony found throughout nature and art. Dividing the frame by this proportion gives a composition greater beauty and visual power.

points.title: Harmonious Proportions
points.body: Golden section divisions create a natural, pleasing relationship between whole and parts.

points.title: Natural Focal Point
points.body: Golden section points anchor the eye and heighten visual appeal.

points.title: Balanced Structure
points.body: Clear hierarchy yields a more balanced, stable spatial distribution.

usage.title: HOW TO APPLY
items: 1 Set frame proportions: divide the frame along a 1 : 1.618 ratio.
2 Locate golden section points: identify the key points along the dividing lines.
3 Place primary visual elements: position the subject or focal point on a golden section point.
4 Refine supporting elements and whitespace: balance the space to reinforce visual rhythm.

003.name: Golden Spiral Composition
003.summary: The Golden Spiral is a visual guide rooted in the Golden Ratio that naturally draws the eye toward the focal point, creating a harmonious, graceful, and vibrant composition.

points.title: Beauty in Nature
points.body: Found widely in nature, such as nautilus shells, sunflowers, and hurricanes.

points.title: Golden Ratio
points.body: Adjacent terms approach a 1:1.618 ratio, establishing harmonious spatial relationships.

points.title: Visual Guidance
points.body: The curve guides the eye smoothly inward to focus on the core of the frame.

points.title: 1 Starting Point
points.body: Beginning at the frame's edge, the curve unfolds naturally to draw the eye in.

points.title: 2 Flow
points.body: The sweep of the curve guides the eye smoothly inward along its path.

points.title: 3 Focus
points.body: The spiral's center serves as the focal point, capturing and holding attention.

points.title: 4 Balance
points.body: The Golden Spiral achieves dynamic balance, keeping the frame stable yet full of tension.

usage.title: TIPS
items: Place the subject or focal point at the spiral's center or a key turning point.
Arrange elements along the spiral curve to avoid rigid, linear layouts.
Whitespace and rhythm matter just as much—give the eye room to breathe.
Practice observing Golden Spirals in nature to build compositional intuition.

notes: THE PRINCIPLE
The ratio of adjacent numbers approaches 1.618 : 1 (the Golden Ratio)
Squares and arcs built from the Fibonacci sequence form the Golden Spiral.
APPLICATIONS
Landscape photography: enhances depth and visual rhythm
Portrait photography: highlights the subject and creates an elegant mood
Graphic design: guides information hierarchy and elevates the visual experience
Film composition: strengthens storytelling and emotional flow

004.name: Golden Triangle Composition
004.summary: Use a primary diagonal and a secondary diagonal to build a stable yet dynamic triangular structure that naturally guides the eye to the key subject.

points.title: Directional Guidance
points.body: Diagonals generate momentum and guide the eye through the frame.

points.title: Focal Point
points.body: Strong intersections concentrate attention and highlight the key subject.

points.title: Visual Tension
points.body: Diagonals and triangles combine to create visual tension.

points.title: Stable Structure
points.body: Triangular geometry anchors the layout for a balanced, grounded feel.

usage.title: Usage Tips
items: Landscape photography: combine the horizon with diagonals, placing the focal point at a strong intersection
Portrait photography: position the subject on an intersection and use background lines to lead the eye
Editorial layout: place key information at intersections to establish clear hierarchy
Product showcase: use diagonals to guide the eye and highlight core selling points

notes: COMPOSITION PRINCIPLES
Use a primary diagonal and an auxiliary line to form a stable yet dynamic triangular structure, naturally guiding the eye to the focal subject.
Key elements of the Golden Triangle
KEY ELEMENTS
Create a sense of direction and enhance visual momentum
Strong intersections act as focal points that hold the viewer's gaze
Build a stable structure to give the frame visual weight
Balance tension and stability for a cohesive, harmonious composition
DIRECTION
FROM LINE TO SHAPE, FROM STRUCTURE TO FOCUS

005.name: Diagonal Method
005.summary: Use diagonals to establish tension and direction, guiding the eye smoothly from one corner to the opposite for greater movement and depth.

points.title: Visual Guidance
points.body: Guides the eye in a clear, intentional flow.

points.title: Heightened Tension
points.body: Breaks stillness and adds kinetic energy.

points.title: Rhythm & Movement
points.body: Arranging elements along the diagonal creates rhythm.

points.title: Angle Selection
points.body: 30°-60° delivers the most comfortable visual balance.

usage.title: TIPS
items: Start from the corners: choose two opposite corners as entry and exit points
Scale contrast: vary element sizes along the line to strengthen spatial depth
Whitespace balance: leave breathing room on both sides of the diagonal to keep the frame balanced

notes: Use the diagonal to build tension and direction, leading the eye naturally from one corner to the opposite, creating movement and depth.
EXAMPLE
Subjects, color blocks, or graphic elements follow the diagonal, forming a visual path from near to far and small to large.
One diagonal line can bring the whole composition to life.

006.name: Rectangle Inset Method
006.summary: Nest rectangular frames layer by layer to build a visual tunnel that emphasizes the subject and draws the eye inward.

points.body: Step inward layer by layer from the outer edge to form a visual tunnel
Control whitespace between layers to maintain breathing room
Place the subject at the center or golden zone to sharpen focus

usage.title: Usage Tips
items: Ideal for product display, portraits, photography, posters, and layouts to create order and sophistication.

notes: LAYER BY LAYER FOCUS INWARD
USE INSET RECTANGLES TO BUILD A VISUAL PATHWAY, ENHANCE THE SUBJECT, AND GUIDE THE EYE INWARD TO THE FOCAL POINT.

007.name: Odd-Number Rule
007.summary: In visual design and layout, grouping an odd number of elements more easily creates rhythm, hierarchy, and a natural viewing experience.

points.title: Dominant Element
points.body: An odd-numbered arrangement naturally establishes one focal point to anchor the eye.

points.title: Supporting Elements
points.body: The remaining elements act as foils, balancing the composition and adding depth.

points.title: Natural Rhythm
points.body: Odd groupings break rigid symmetry, adding cadence and vitality.

points.title: Why Odd Numbers?
points.body: Odd groupings more easily create a natural focal point and preserve breathing room, avoiding the stiffness of equal splits.

usage.title: Usage Tips
items: Favor groupings of 3 or 5 elements.
Define one dominant element and let the rest support it.
Create variation through scale, placement, or color.

008.name: Space Rule
008.summary: Use whitespace and spatial proportion purposefully so key content stands out naturally, giving information breathing room and clear hierarchy.

points.title: Whitespace
points.body: Generous negative space keeps the composition clean and comfortable.

points.title: Contrast
points.body: Pairing small elements with expansive space naturally creates a focal point.

points.title: Proportion
points.body: Thoughtful spatial proportions establish a clear information hierarchy.

notes: USE NEGATIVE SPACE AND PROPORTION TO CREATE EMPHASIS, BREATH, AND HIERARCHY.
THE CORE OF SPACE CONTROL
KEYWORDS
Create calm and breathing room
Highlight key points and draw attention
Give information comfortable separation
Establish reading order through spatial scale and placement
SPACE IS NOT EMPTY, BUT THE STAGE FOR WHAT MATTERS.

009.name: Eye Room
009.summary: Leave open space in the direction the subject is looking to make the frame more comfortable and breathable.

points.title: Key Principles
points.body: • Leave enough space in the direction of gaze to avoid crowding or visual pressure. • Whitespace guides the eye, enhancing rhythm and depth. • Giving the viewer room to breathe makes communication more natural and effective.

usage.title: APPLICATIONS
items: PHOTOGRAPHY
VIDEO
ADVERTISING
PRESENTATION

notes: LEAVE SPACE IN THE DIRECTION OF GAZE TO CREATE A MORE COMPORTABLE AND BREATHABLE COMPOSITION.

010.name: Motion Space
010.summary: When a subject implies movement, leave open space ahead of its path to make the frame more comfortable, dynamic, and intuitive.

points.title: Direction
points.body: Leave space wherever the subject is heading.

points.title: Speed
points.body: The faster the motion, the more space should open up ahead.

points.title: Anticipation
points.body: Reserve space in advance to guide the viewer's eye.

points.title: Balance
points.body: Keep the lead space visually balanced against the subject's size.

notes: LEAVE SPACE AHEAD OF MOVEMENT
LEAD ROOM: Reserve space ahead of motion so direction reads clearly and the message is easy to grasp.

011.name: Header Space Composition
011.summary: Leave generous empty space at the top of the frame so the eye settles naturally downward, spotlighting the subject and establishing clear hierarchy and rhythm.

points.title: Hierarchy
points.body: Establishes visual priority

points.title: Breathing Room

points.title: Focus
points.body: Concentrates viewer attention

points.title: Calm

usage.title: Key Principle
items: The more whitespace above, the more prominent the subject—giving the frame breathing room and a refined feel.

notes: Leave ample header space to create ease and poise.

012.name: Fill the Frame
012.summary: Let the subject fill the entire frame to maximize visual impact.

points.title: Immersion
points.body: The subject extends to the edges, minimizing background distractions and drawing the viewer in.

points.title: Tension
points.body: With the subject occupying the whole frame, compressed space builds urgency and force.

points.title: Impact
points.body: Magnifies detail and form, boosting visual weight to grab attention instantly.

usage.title: Usage Tips
items: Ideal for highlighting a single subject, conveying emotion, setting a mood, or emphasizing a central theme.

013.name: Negative Space Composition
013.summary: Use the empty space (negative space) around the subject to shape form and convey meaning, making emptiness an essential part of the frame.

points.title: Key Tip
points.body: Strip away unnecessary elements so whitespace serves the theme, sharpening visual focus and expression.

095.name: Visual Hierarchy
095.summary: Organizes information into clear tiers to guide the eye, highlight key messages, and speed up comprehension for clearer, more effective communication.

points.title: Primary Level
points.body: Most important information: uses the largest type, strongest contrast, and most prominent placement to capture attention, establish the focal point, and deliver the core theme.

points.title: Secondary Level

points.title: Tertiary Level
points.body: Supplementary details: uses smaller type, lower contrast, and secondary placement to provide supporting context without competing for attention.

usage.title: Design Principles
items: 1. Reading Order: Top to bottom, left to right, large to small, strong to subtle—guiding the reading flow naturally.
2. Visual Prominence: Create differentiation through scale, color, contrast, and whitespace to spotlight the most critical information.
3. Scanning Path: Align with F-pattern or Z-pattern scanning habits, placing key information at anchor points along the path.
4. Measured Emphasis: Highlight priorities without over-decorating so every tier remains clear and rhythmic.

096.name: Primary & Secondary Relationship
096.summary: In a layout, primary-secondary relationships use contrast and harmony so key information stands out while supporting details reinforce it in order, creating clear visual hierarchy and efficient communication.

points.title: Establish Dominance
points.body: Use larger scale, higher contrast, stronger color, or a central position to establish the focal point.

points.title: Supporting Role
points.body: Secondary elements use smaller scale, softer contrast, and lighter visual weight to support and complement the primary element.

points.title: Reinforce with Contrast
points.body: Apply contrast in scale, color, value, density, and placement to sharpen the distinction between primary and secondary elements.

points.title: Cohesive Harmony
points.body: Maintain consistent style, palette, or rhythm across contrasting elements so the layout stays unified and ordered.

usage.title: Contrast Toolkit
items: Scale Contrast: Primary elements are larger; secondary elements are smaller.
Color Contrast: Primary elements are bolder; secondary elements are more muted.
Value Contrast: Primary elements are brighter or darker to anchor focus.
Density Contrast: Primary elements have more breathing room; secondary elements sit closer together.
Position Contrast: Primary elements occupy prime positions; secondary elements sit around them.
Form Contrast: Primary elements are more distinctive; secondary elements are more uniform.

notes: Comparison
Clear Hierarchy: Defined focal point, distinct tiers, and a smooth reading path.
Muddled Hierarchy: Similar visual weights blur hierarchy and reduce communication efficiency.
Design Tip: Define the primary message first, then arrange supporting elements so the eye locks onto the core before flowing through the details.

Exponential distribution (waiting time): the longer an event has not occurred, the more likely it is to occur. Uniform distribution (equally likely): every outcome has the same chance of occurring.
What can we know? Likelihood of occurrence · Long-term average trends · Risk of extreme events · Scope of impact on the system

Modeling methods: Discrete random variables: enumerable outcomes, such as coin flips. Continuous random variables: outcomes within a range, such as height or temperature. Markov process: the future depends only on the current state. Monte Carlo simulation: approximating real results through large numbers of random trials.
Randomness ≠ Chaos: Fully ordered: predictable, lacking flexibility. Moderately random: balances stability with adaptability. Completely random: unstructured and inefficient.
